title: A Phase 2 Clinical Study of MIL62 in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
off: A Phase 2 Clinical Study to Evaluate the Safety and Efficacy of Recombinant Humanized Monoclonal Antibody MIL62 Injection in the Treatment of Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.
summary: This study will evaluate the efficacy, safety, pharmacokinetics(PK), pharmacodynamics(PD) and ADA of MIL62 compared with placebo in participants with systemic lupus erythematosus.

primary.m: Part A and Part B:Percentage of participants achieving SRI-4 at Week 12

pubs.cit: Li Y, Shi G, Jiang G, Wei M, Liu Z, Wu Q, et al. Efficacy and safety of obinutuzumab β in patients with active systemic lupus erythematosus: a multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 2 trial. Lancet Rheumatol. 2026. doi: 10.1016/S2665-9913(26)00315-2

abstracts:
Li Y, Shi G, Jiang G, Wei M, Liu Z, Wu Q, et al. Efficacy and safety of obinutuzumab β in patients with active systemic lupus erythematosus: a multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 2 trial. Lancet Rheumatol. 2026. doi: 10.1016/S2665-9913(26)00315-2
BACKGROUND: B cells play a central role in the pathogenesis of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and are a therapeutic target. We therefore assessed the efficacy and safety of obinutuzumab β, a glycoengineered type II anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody, in patients with active SLE.
METHODS: In this multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 2 trial, we enrolled patients who were aged 18-80 years, fulfilled the 2019 European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology-American College of Rheumatology classification criteria for SLE, and had active disease (defined as a Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Disease Activity Index 2000 [SLEDAI-2K] score of 8 or more and positivity for antinuclear antibodies or anti-double stranded DNA antibodies) at 30 tertiary hospitals in China. Participants were randomly allocated 1:1 to receive obinutuzumab β or placebo, stratified by SLEDAI-2K score and 24-h urine protein level. Patients, investigators, and the sponsor were masked to treatment allocation. Patients received intravenous infusions of obinutuzumab β (1000 mg) or placebo on days 1, 15, 169, 183, 365, and 379. All patients maintained their background standard therapy. The primary efficacy endpoint was the proportion of patients with an SLE Responder Index (SRI)-4 response at week 12 assessed in all patients who were randomly assigned and received at least one dose of study treatment (ie, the full analysis set). Safety was assessed in all patients who received any study treatment and had at least one post-dose safety assessment (ie, the safety analysis set) over 52 weeks. The study was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05796206) and is complete. People with lived experience were not involved as research partners in this study.
FINDINGS: Between May 26, 2023, and July 29, 2024, 171 patients were screened for eligibility. Of these, 123 patients were randomly assigned to receive obinutuzumab β (n=61) or placebo (n=62) and were included in both the full analysis set and safety analysis sets. The mean age was 36·1 years (SD 10·3). 115 (93%) of 123 patients were female, eight (7%) were male, and 117 (95%) were Han Chinese ethnicity. At week 12, 32 (52%) of 61 patients in the obinutuzumab β group and 21 (34%) of 62 in the placebo group had an SRI-4 response (adjusted risk difference 19 percentage points, 95% CI 3-36; p=0·022). Serious adverse events occurred in 12 (20%) patients in the obinutuzumab β group and 14 (23%) in the placebo group. One fatal treatment-emergent adverse event (sepsis) occurred in the placebo group.
INTERPRETATION: Obinutuzumab β plus standard therapy improved SRI-4 response at week 12 in Chinese patients with active SLE, with a generally manageable safety profile over 52 weeks. These phase 2 findings support further evaluation and longer-term safety follow-up.
FUNDING: Beijing Mabworks Biotech.

x.titre: MIL62 contre placebo dans le lupus systémique
x.question: L'anticorps anti-CD20 MIL62 augmente-t-il la proportion de réponse SRI-4 à 12 semaines dans le lupus systémique ?
x.contexte:
Le lupus systémique actif reste difficile à contrôler malgré l'hydroxychloroquine, les corticoïdes, les immunosuppresseurs et le bélimumab. La déplétion des lymphocytes B est une stratégie plausible, mais les essais du rituximab n'ont pas atteint leurs critères principaux.

Le MIL62 est un anticorps anti-CD20 humanisé et glyco-modifié, conçu pour une cytotoxicité cellulaire plus forte que celle du rituximab. Cette étude de phase 2, randomisée en double aveugle contre placebo, a inclus 123 adultes de 18 à 80 ans, dans un centre chinois (promoteur : Mabworks). Elle comporte les parties A et B. Elle évalue aussi la pharmacocinétique, la pharmacodynamique et les anticorps anti-médicament.
x.interet: Elle permettra de savoir si cette déplétion B plus puissante apporte une réponse dans le lupus actif, avant un éventuel essai de phase 3.
x.profil: Des adultes de 18 à 80 ans atteints de lupus systémique actif sous traitement stable.
inclusion: Anticorps antinucléaires ≥ 1/80 ou anti-ADN natif positif
Traitement stable depuis au moins 30 jours
exclusion: Rituximab ou autre déplétion B dans les 9 mois
Cyclophosphamide dans les 8 semaines, inhibiteurs de calcineurine ou échanges plasmatiques dans les 4 semaines
Bélimumab ou télitacicept dans les 12 semaines, anti-TNF, anti-JAK ou thalidomide dans les 4 semaines
Hépatite B (ADN élevé), hépatite C ou VIH
Allergie sévère aux anticorps monoclonaux humanisés, grossesse ou allaitement

bras.traitement: MIL62 par voie injectable (parties A et B)

x.critere: Proportion de patients atteignant une réponse SRI-4 à la semaine 12.
x.resultats: Cet essai de phase 2 randomisé en double aveugle a inclus 123 patients lupiques actifs dans 30 centres chinois (61 sous obinutuzumab β, 62 sous placebo), en plus du traitement de fond. À la semaine 12, une réponse SRI-4 était obtenue chez 32 patients (52 %) sous obinutuzumab β contre 21 (34 %) sous placebo, soit une différence ajustée de 19 points (IC 95 % 3-36 ; p = 0,022). Des événements indésirables graves sont survenus chez 12 patients (20 %) sous obinutuzumab β et 14 (23 %) sous placebo sur 52 semaines. Un décès par sepsis est survenu dans le groupe placebo. Les auteurs concluent que l'obinutuzumab β améliore la réponse SRI-4 à 12 semaines avec une tolérance globalement acceptable, et justifie des évaluations plus longues.
